title: Cost drilldown cross-filter prototype: stitch patterns and visual redlines
creator: Diego Marquez
description:
Goal: Finalize visual and interaction patterns for the compact cost drilldown panel that supports cross-filtering between time-series, model variants, and rollout segments. This ticket collects final redlines from design reviews, records stakeholder decisions, and bundles QA handoff materials for engineering and product. The core challenge is preserving glanceable cost attribution while enabling fast, reversible cross-filters without overwhelming the density of the console view.

Scope and deliverables:
- High-fidelity Figma frames for the compact drilldown modal (desktop/tablet) showing cross-filter flows when a user toggles: timeframe, model family, rollout variant, and region.
- Annotated redlines (spacing, contrast, hover & focus states, microcopy) and an accessibility checklist (color contrast numbers, keyboard focus order).
- Interactive prototype demonstrating: selecting a time window, adding/removing a variant filter, and a clear "revert filters" affordance.
- A short QA checklist and known edge cases for the first engineering pass (prefetch behavior for filters, empty states, animation fallback).

Design constraints and considerations:
- Maintain parity with the compact cost tile visual language used elsewhere in Console; but reduce vertical height by 20% to fit glance grid.
- Hover states should use 2px subtle elevation + 6% darker neutral border rather than large shadows to avoid visual noise.
- Cross-filter toggles need explicit microcopy for ambiguous variants (e.g., "small-batch" vs "small_batch") and a normalization rule must be enforced in the API contract.

Out of scope for this ticket: backend aggregation changes, dedicated mobile styling beyond responsive breakpoints.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Figma frames include final redlines with measurements and token references for spacing, border, and type; 2) Interactive prototype (FigJam or InVision link) demonstrates filter add/remove/revert with realistic timing; 3) Accessibility checklist passed: text/icon contrast >= 4.5:1 for primary actions, keyboard nav order documented; 4) QA checklist attached and engineering has acknowledged handoff in the sync channel; 5) Known edge-cases documented with mitigation recommendations.
